teaser: Anthropic's Scion replaced Git for agents inside one company; sgit, open source and encrypted, shares its core ideas. Revised and re-measured.
core_idea: Agents broke Git's offline, full-clone assumptions at Anthropic, which built Scion: a server that does history, blame, merges and commits, immutable objects served from cache tiers, and clients that fetch only what they need; sgit reaches the same properties from the opposite design, a dumb server that stores encrypted objects named by their ciphertext, reads from any static host and objects any cache can keep, and scoped, shallow and on-demand clones, measured on the 35,000-object vault the newsroom's agents share; Scion is ahead on server-side history, merge, blame and proven scale, but it is internal, while sgit is open source and encrypts everything.

nodes.label: Scion: the server does the work
nodes.summary: History, blame, merges server-side; cache tiers; no full copy.

nodes.label: sgit: a dumb, blind server
nodes.summary: Client encrypts, merges and verifies; server stores ciphertext.

nodes.label: Immutable ids that cache
nodes.summary: SHA-256 of the ciphertext; the name says -imm-, so anyone can keep them.

nodes.label: Reads from any GET host
nodes.summary: --transport static; no sgit server in the path.

nodes.label: Measured on a busy vault
nodes.summary: 35,000 objects: one folder, one commit, 13 s; the 59 s was a bug.

nodes.label: Where Scion is ahead
nodes.summary: Server-side blame and bisect; proven scale; history walked per commit.

nodes.label: Git side by side
nodes.summary: Coexist in a folder; no history bridge.

nodes.label: Internal versus open
nodes.summary: Scion unreleased; sgit on PyPI today.
